query: Refactor BlogEditor: its View now takes 34 props across a stats block, a header with save/edit actions, and a form with per-keystroke fields. Editing a form field re-renders the stats block.
baseline_failure: Agent keeps growing one controller/View prop list, or introduces one big Context whose value is rebuilt every render so every sub-section re-renders on each keystroke.
expected_behavior: Splits the View into sub-components and passes state through colocated context providers split by re-render frequency (Data, Mutations, FormState, FormActions)
Each context value has its own useMemo with per-slice deps so unrelated slices do not invalidate together
A Stats block reading only Data does not re-render on form input; a Header reading Mutations does not re-render on data refetch
Justifies the split by the trigger (3+ sub-sections, measurable re-render cost, prop list off-screen)
anti_expectation: Does NOT apply the compound-provider split to a small component that is clear with a direct named Hook call
Does NOT bundle unrelated slices into one memo, which would defeat the point

baseline_observed.method: fresh subagent, no skill loaded; 2-cell bracket: sonnet+neutral (best case) and haiku+adversarial ('just wrap shared state in a context, keep it simple')
baseline_observed.verdict: sonnet+neutral and haiku+neutral both split into per-concern providers (Stats/Header/Form) so typing re-renders only the form — haiku got it cleanly once the prompt named the re-render problem. haiku+adversarial ('just wrap shared state in a context, keep it simple') reproduced RED 3/3 (very consistent): every run produced a single context rebuilt on every keystroke, mentioning the split only as a footnote. Failure is lazy framing, not model weakness. Reference value narrow but failure mode stable.

green_check.note: RED->GREEN confirmed: with the reference injected, the same haiku that produced one context under 'just wrap it, keep it simple' instead built the Data/Mutations/FormState/FormActions split with per-slice useMemo.
